Future Hungary–Ukraine relations will be defined by Ukraine’s implementation of the minority rights agreement, with legislative progress expected in October. A failure to implement the deal could risk slowing down Kyiv’s EU path and decoupling the Ukrainian and Moldovan accession bids.

latest_rss.title: Having Lost ‘Presidents,’ Ever More Russian Federal Subjects Now Have Prime Ministers
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




At Russian President Vladimir Putin’s insistence, Russia has only one president. Since his war against Ukraine began in 2022, the number of federal subjects with prime ministers in addition to Moscow-appointed “heads” has risen from 10 to 39 and is likely to continue to rise.



This change, which has largely been under the radar, reflects the increasing burdens Putin’s policies have shifted to the federal subjects and the desire of their heads to share these and the challenges anger about them now pose.



As a result, the governments of the federal subjects are looking like self-standing institutions even though Moscow appoints their heads and thus may have a greater capacity to act as independent actors in the course of the looming succession struggle.

latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Russian military doctrine proposed a Fire Engagement Complex (FEC) linking sensors, artificial intelligence, communications, navigation, and weapons into a software-defined network designed to dramatically compress the detect-to-strike cycle.



Frontline forces are already improvising sensor-to-shooter networks, combining fiber-optic first-person view (FPV) drones, reconnaissance systems, electronic maps, radar, and mobile fire teams to create effective but largely manual kill chains.

latest_rss.summary: From the air, they look like something out of science fiction: perfect green circles stamped into an ocean of sand, each one nearly a kilometer across, neatly arranged along the southern edge of China's largest desert, the Taklimakan. Across the southern edge of the Taklimakan Desert, 35,000 mu (over 23 square kilometers) of winter wheat is being sown in fields shaped like perfect circles. The seed drills are guided by Beidou, China's satellite navigation system, and local authorities expect planting to be completed around October 20.The circles are the signature of center-pivot irrigation. A long sprinkler arm rotates around a central point, drawing water from snowmelt in the Kunlun Mountains and spreading it evenly across land that was once rolling sand dunes.
